articles.title: When the shoreline moves: What happens to Kerala’s coastal communities?
articles.excerpt: Kerala’s coastal communities face a dire crisis as relentless erosion reshapes the shoreline, threatening homes, livelihoods, and freshwater reserves. In Pozhiyoor, families live on the edge, with seawalls failing to protect against advancing waves. The state’s relocation initiatives offer temporary relief, but challenges like inadequate housing and strained resources persist, leaving many struggling to adapt to a rapidly changing landscape.

articles.excerpt: About one in five food samples tested in India in 2024–25 failed to meet standards. articles.title: India’s TB Burden Declines, but Elimination Targets Remain Distant
articles.excerpt: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the global tuberculosis (TB) burden, despite gradual improvements in disease incidence and mortality. The estimated incidence rate declined from 237 cases per lakh population in 2015 to 187 in 2024, while mortality fell from 28 to 21 deaths per lakh. However, both remain substantially higher than the targets set under the National Strategic Plan for TB Elimination 2017–2025.
articles.author: Sai Krishna Muthyanolla

articles.excerpt: India's 2026 southwest monsoon ended with 759.4 mm of rainfall, just 87% of the Long Period Average (LPA), making it the 13th-weakest season since 1901. But the national deficit tells only part of the story. Rainfall was unevenly distributed, with 44% of districts recording deficient or large deficient rainfall, the highest share since 2015. Of the 36 meteorological subdivisions, 30 received less rain than in 2025.

articles.excerpt: India recorded 3,253 stampede deaths between 2001 and 2024, with men accounting for 68% of fatalities during this period. However, the pattern shifted sharply in 2024, when women made up 87% of the 147 deaths recorded. Between 2014 and 2024, adults aged 30–45 accounted for the largest share of fatalities, followed by people aged 60 and above.
